To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

'By exploiting the physical properties, such as softness and plasticity, of continuous materials such as clay or sand, it is feasible to bridge the gap between physical and digital design and to create new types of tangible user interfaces for design and analysis.'

(i) continuous physical materials, such as clay and wet sand, can be used to create tangible user interfaces that enable the direct manipulation of digital information and computational analysis, (ii) these new TUIs offer rapid physical form giving in combination computational feedback, (iii) they are suitable for use in a wide variety of applications, such as design and education, and (iv) they have the potential to revolutionise the way we design.
we have developed a new generation of tangible user interfaces, termed Continuous TUIs, that enable dynamic sculptural form giving in combination and feedback with computational analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploration and development of a novel class of TUIs for the creation of dynamic, interactive, and computational forms.
the development of a new type of TUI, the continuous tangible user interface (cTUI), which combines the physical properties of clay and sand with computational analysis.
developing new TUI technologies to enable designers to work in a more natural and creative way with digital tools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Continuous TUIs offer a new way to interact with computational design systems and to manipulate and analyse physical materials.
Continuous TUIs are an effective means of enabling designers and architects to explore and manipulate the physical properties of materials in a digital design environment.
Continuous TUIs are a new class of interfaces that enable dynamic sculptural design and computational analysis using physically augmented continuous materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are bringing back clay and sand into digital design.
the combination of physical and computational materials and tools is a promising direction for future TUI research.
the combination of digital and continuous physical materials can provide a powerful new design medium for landscape architecture and urban design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
continuous TUIs offer a new approach to design that is based on the physical manipulation of soft materials and the computational analysis of the resulting forms.
continuous TUIs are a new class of interfaces that can be applied to many domains and that can be used to create new types of design tools.

the use of soft continuous materials in digital design can enable a new generation of tangible interfaces that can support a wide range of applications in the design process, from concept generation and exploration to detailed analysis and evaluation.
